## Functions or modules to implement
No code changes. Two data/doc edits:

1. **Create `.github/ai/alert_inbox.json`.** This is the config file that `scripts/alert_inbox_capture.sh` reads (`_ALERT_INBOX_CONFIG_REL=".github/ai/alert_inbox.json"`, line 36). Its header says "Both switches ship as false". Use 2-space JSON indentation, like the other `.github/ai/*.json` files, and end the file with a newline. Content, taken from `docs/plans/alert-triage-auto-heal-plan.md` (lines 238-244, 308-316, 371-376):
   - `"capture_enabled": false`
   - `"route_warning_error_to_inbox": false`
   - `"pipeline_self_files"`: `.github/workflows/implement.yml`, `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`, `.github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml`, `.github/workflows/clarify.yml`, `.github/workflows/plan.yml`, `.github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml`, `.github/workflows/workflow-failure-heal-intake.yml`, `.github/workflows/alert-triage.yml`, `.github/workflows/alert-self-fix.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/ai_engine.sh`, `scripts/claude_pool_token.sh`, `scripts/review_head_gate.sh`, `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh`, `scripts/tg_helpers.sh`
   - `"break_glass_allowed_paths"`: `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `scripts/**`, `prompts/**`, `tests/**`, `changelog.d/*.md`, `agents.d/*.md`
   - `"break_glass_denied_paths"`: `.github/ai/**`, `.claude/**`, `CLAUDE.md`, `unattended_system_instructions.md`, `tools/**`, `scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py`, `scripts/alert_self_fix_break_glass.sh`
   - No other keys. The plan doc's Phase 1 shape names only the two switches; the three list keys are the ones `test_shipped_config_is_off` requires.

2. **Add four entries to `docs/INVENTORY.md`.** `tests/inventory_parity.py` compares sets, so order is not enforced. Keep the existing alphabetical placement anyway.
   - Under `## Workflows`, right after the `.github/workflows/ci.yml` line (line 55):
     `` - `.github/workflows/ci_pr_quick.yml` — GitHub Actions workflow: CI quick; per-push static checks (`quick / <job>` check-runs) for every PR, while the full `ci.yml` suite runs once per PR head at the end of review (cut-ci-runner-time Phase 4). ``
   - Under `## Scripts`, right after `scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py` (line 147):
     `` - `scripts/ci_docs_only_paths.sh` — Docs-only final CI path list: `classify` decides whether a PR's changed files are all docs-only, so the final `ci.yml` dispatch passes `docs_only=true`; `verify` re-checks the merge tree in the `lint` job (Refs #9528). ``
   - Under `## Scripts`, after the `scripts/review_autofix_step_*` block and before the next `scripts/review_*` entry, keeping alphabetical order:
     `` - `scripts/review_final_ci_failed.sh` — Body of `ci.yml`'s `final-ci-failed` job: when a final-CI dispatch run's `lint` fails, posts one `ai:final-ci-failed:v1` marker comment per head and re-dispatches the PR's review (`FINAL_CI_FAILED_REDISPATCH_ENABLED`). ``
     `` - `scripts/review_final_ci_sweep.sh` — Review-sweep safety net: each tick, hands open PR heads whose review gate passed but that never got a final CI run to `_pr_ensure_final_ci` (`REVIEW_FINAL_CI_WORKFLOW`, `FINAL_CI_SWEEP_MAX_PER_TICK`). ``
   - Each description contains no other `scripts/...` or `.github/workflows/...` path tokens beyond ones the inventory already documents (`ci.yml`). This avoids triggering new "unexpected tracked-surface reference" failures.

## Data structures affected
- New JSON config `.github/ai/alert_inbox.json`: two booleans plus three non-empty string arrays. The capture code treats a missing or invalid file as "off", so shipping it as all-off changes no runtime behaviour.
- `docs/INVENTORY.md` roster: four added lines.

## API or interface changes
None. Both switches stay `false`, so `alert_inbox_mode` still resolves to `off` (see `test_shipped_config_resolves_off`). No env vars, labels or workflow inputs change.

## Decisions
### D1 — Ship the config with both switches off and the plan's list values
- Chosen: Create `.github/ai/alert_inbox.json` exactly as in the issue's suggested fix, with values taken from `docs/plans/alert-triage-auto-heal-plan.md`.
- Alternatives considered: Relax or skip `test_shipped_config_is_off`; ship only the two booleans.
- Why: The issue forbids skipping the test, and the test requires the three non-empty lists. Taking the values from the reviewed plan doc keeps Phase 2/3 consumers consistent, and both switches off keeps consumers unaffected.

### D2 — Fix the inherited inventory drift in this PR
- Chosen: Add the four `docs/INVENTORY.md` entries on `ai/issue-9395`.
- Alternatives considered: Fix it only on `orchestrator/project-9394` or main, and leave PR #9401 red.
- Why: Implement can only write to this PR's branch. The entries are additive docs, and a later sync from main that adds the same lines resolves trivially. `isolated-base` (the default branch) lacks them too, so main will need the same lines; that is noted as a risk rather than added to scope.

### D3 — Leave the label contract alone
- Chosen: Make no change to `.github/ai/label_contract.v1.json`.
- Alternatives considered: Add `ai:alert-triage` and `ai:alert-self-fix`, as the issue suggests as a possibility.
- Why: Both labels are already in the contract (`label_contract.v1.json:228` and `:232`), so the suspected third failure does not exist on this head.

## Security considerations
- Trust boundary: `.github/ai/alert_inbox.json` is a trusted input. The capture code reads it only from trusted support roots, never from the caller's checkout. Shipping both switches `false` means no alert text is dispatched anywhere. The break-glass deny list keeps `.github/ai/**`, `.claude/**`, `CLAUDE.md`, the auto-close linter and the break-glass script itself out of self-fix reach. This matters for Phase 3 abuse resistance: a self-fix PR must not be able to widen its own allow-list.
- No new endpoints or surfaces, and no secrets in either file.
- The automation-path guard needs `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=true` plus a grant to stage `.github/ai/alert_inbox.json`. This issue has no `files_touched` block. If it was authored by the GH_PAT login (the triage bot), it gets the `pipeline_author_no_allowlist` open grant; otherwise the guard drops the file (see Risks).

## Potential risks or edge cases
- **Automation-path guard drops the file again.** This is the likely root cause of the original omission. If the implement run's guard reports `IMPLEMENT_AUTOMATION_PATH_GUARD` blocking `.github/ai/alert_inbox.json`, the result is `ai:scope-blocked`, and the file has to land from an interactive session (the issue's stated fallback).
- **Conflict with the issue text:** the issue suggests a possible label-contract gap. The repo shows both labels already present, so there is nothing to do.
- **Sandbox artefact:** running `tests/inventory_parity.py` in this snapshot also reports `unexpected tracked-surface reference .github/workflows/propagate-consumer-secrets.yml`. The snapshot filters that file out because of its name; it is in the inventory (`docs/INVENTORY.md:90`) and on `isolated-base`, and the CI log doesn't show the error. Do not remove that inventory line.
- **Merge conflicts:** several open PRs (#9359, #9601, #9510, …) touch `docs/INVENTORY.md`, and one of them may add the same four lines. Conflicts are additive one-liners.
- Main (`isolated-base`) also lacks the four entries, so other PRs keep failing until main is fixed. That is out of scope here.

## Testing considerations
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_tg_helpers_alert_inbox.py` (CI runs it at `ci.yml:1525`). `test_shipped_config_is_off` goes from red to green, and `test_shipped_config_resolves_off` must stay `off`.
- `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/inventory_parity.py` (CI at `ci.yml:2696`). The four "missing" lines and the six README/agents.md cross-reference failures disappear. In the sandbox, the `propagate-consumer-secrets.yml` lines remain because of the filtered snapshot (see Risks).
- `python3 -m json.tool .github/ai/alert_inbox.json` confirms the JSON is valid.
- No new test files. Do not modify or skip existing tests.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends docs/INVENTORY.md
Scope-mode justification: The issue names two concrete failures: a missing shipped config, and four missing inventory rows. The fix adds exactly those two artefacts, reusing the existing inventory roster and the config shape already defined in the alert-triage plan doc and pinned by `test_shipped_config_is_off`. Under §6 (Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed), shipping the complete config, including the plan-doc lists rather than placeholder values, costs only a few lines and is the more correct option, so it is chosen.
